newsitem.title: USA: NLRB to file against Gannett, Knight-Ridder.
newsitem.headline: NLRB to file against Gannett, Knight-Ridder.

text.p: The National Labor Relations Board said Tuesday that it will seek a federal court order early next week requiring the Detroit Free Press, The Detroit News, and Detroit Newspapers, the agency that publishes both papers under a joint-operating agreement, to rehire workers who struck the papers in July 1995.
The board had ruled earlier that the companies had taken part in unfair labor practices.
The NLRB said that it would also ask that replacement workers hired by the newspapers be dismissed, if necessary, to make room for the strikers.

The board said its expects to file a petition for injunctive relief in the U.S. District Court in Detroit under a section of the National Labor Relations Act that allows it to ask the court to stop unfair labor practices.

The usual procedure, said the NLRB, is that a judge is assigned upon the filing of the petition and will determine the schedule for further proceedings. The injunction, said the board, can be appealed if it is granted.
